title: AGAPE saints and feasts, all traditions (agape-saints/1)
description: Every fixed commemoration of the Eastern Orthodox, Catholic and Coptic Orthodox calendars in one shape. Dates are stored in each tradition's own calendar; tools/build_unified_saints.py resolves them for a given day (see saint_day.schema.json).

dated_readings.description: Readings that follow the lectionary cycle rather than a saint, per tradition and civil date (YYYY-MM-DD). Now only Catholic, 2025-2027.

tradition.description: eastern_orthodox = Tradition.EASTERN_ORTHODOX, catholic = Tradition.CATHOLIC, coptic_orthodox = Tradition.ORIENTAL_ORTHODOX in the app.

source_id.description: The id of an entry in the file's sources list.

licence.description: SPDX id where there is one (MIT, CC0-1.0), 'Public domain', 'AGAPE' for the app's own text, or 'unknown'.

date_rule.description: A fixed date in the tradition's own calendar. 'church' is the Byzantine menologion date: read as Gregorian on the new (Revised Julian) calendar and as Julian on the old calendar.

month.description: 13 is the Coptic little month Nasie.

code.description: The rank as the source writes it: great, major, saint (menologion); solemnity, feast, memorial, optional memorial, commemoration (Roman).

level.description: 1 great feast / solemnity, 2 feast, 3 memorial / saint, 4 optional memorial, 5 commemoration.

life.description: The life (Synaxarion / Martyrologium) or a short summary of it.

scope.description: 'day' when the text speaks of all commemorations of the day (the menologion summaries).

url.description: Where the full text can be read, when it is not bundled.

asset.description: Path inside the app's assets, e.g. icons/nativity.jpg.

url.description: Direct link to the image (Commons Special:FilePath).

page.description: The image's page at its source, for the credit.

fallback.description: A generic icon (a martyr, a bishop), used only when no specific one matches.

match.description: Only in a resolved day: how the icon was chosen.

key.description: The key of an entry in icons.

role.description: Catholic: first_reading..gospel. Byzantine: epistle/apostle, gospel, old_testament (vespers), matins_gospel. Coptic Katameros: pauline, catholic_epistle, acts, psalm_gospel, gospel.

ref.description: The app's own notation (BOOK C:V-V, book ids from books.json), where the reader opens: the first piece of a citation in several pieces, without verse letters. Absent when the citation is too complex.

display.description: The citation as the source writes it.

service.description: Liturgy, Matins, Vespers, ... when the source says.

ref.description: The same commemoration in another dataset, to fetch more (full life, readings) from it later.

score.description: How well the names matched (shared words, Jaccard) when the link was made automatically; absent when set by hand.

provenance.description: Which source each part of the entry comes from.

id.description: tradition/MM-DD/order-slug, MM-DD in the tradition's own calendar.

kind.description: feast: of the Lord, the Mother of God or the Cross; event: council, consecration, translation of relics, miracle; otherwise saint. Derived from the name.

order.description: Position among the day's commemorations in the source; 0 is the principal one.

icon.description: A link to icons in the dataset, the full icon in a resolved day.

readings.description: Proper readings of this commemoration, when it has its own.
